pairs.title: Wavefront sets, Hadamard kernels and admissible local products

A.title: Wavefront and positive-frequency Hadamard data
A.statement: For a distribution u on a smooth manifold, WF(u) consists of nonzero covectors at which no localized Fourier transform decays rapidly in a conic neighborhood. A scalar Hadamard bisolution W on a globally hyperbolic spacetime has WF(W)={(x,k;y,-l):(x,k)~(y,l), k future null}; ~ denotes null-geodesic cotangent transport. The field operator, sign convention and antisymmetric part iΔ must be fixed separately.
A.proof_route: Define chart localization and all conic seminorms, verify chart invariance by nonstationary phase; define geodesic relation without claiming existence of W.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

A.title: Product and pullback under wavefront transversality
A.statement: If u,v are distributions and no (x,k) in WF(u) has (x,-k) in WF(v), their product is a distribution, agrees with multiplication of smooth functions, and has wavefront contained in the nonzero covector sums of WF(u) union the zero section and WF(v) union the zero section. A pullback f*u exists when WF(u) misses the conormal obstruction N_f.
A.proof_route: Partition into compact chart patches; split Fourier convolution into cones on which at least one factor has arbitrary decay, estimate against finite-order growth of the other; prove continuity in the corresponding wavefront topology. Apply to diagonal pullback of u⊗v. This is a new substantive proof obligation, not an unnamed theorem citation.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

A.title: Smooth Hadamard change gives equivalent Wick algebras
A.statement: For two scalar Hadamard two-point distributions W,W′ with the same antisymmetric part and positive-frequency relation, their difference is smooth. On compactly supported polynomial microcausal functionals, contraction products are defined coefficientwise and exp(ℏ〈W′−W,δ²〉/2) intertwines the two products.
A.proof_route: First show the difference is symmetric; symmetry reverses the future relation into the past relation, whose intersection is empty, so its wavefront is empty. For each finite polynomial degree expand contractions and verify the intertwiner by the binomial identity. Specify microcausal derivative wavefront exclusions and compact support; no product on the diagonal is inferred without the wavefront check.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

B.title: Delta-square is outside the product contract
B.statement: The diagonal product δ_0² is not furnished by the wavefront product theorem: WF(δ_0) contains opposite nonzero covectors. A mollifier square has mass proportional to ε^{-n}, and no distribution limit exists without subtraction.
B.proof_route: Compute ∫ε^{-2n}ρ(x/ε)²f(x)dx=ε^{-n}∫ρ(y)²f(εy)dy for nonnegative ρ and f=1 near zero.

pairs.title: All-order scalar causal extension and finite renormalization

A.title: Local scalar time-ordered product contract
A.statement: On flat four-dimensional Minkowski space take compactly supported local polynomial scalar functionals, formal parameters g and ℏ, and the off-shell free field algebra. A renormalization prescription is a family T_n, T_0=1,T_1 fixed, satisfying symmetry, causal factorization, translation covariance, field independence, the stated scaling bound, and formal unitarity. Gauge identities are additional conditions.
A.proof_route: Specify variational derivative wavefronts, relative coordinates at each total diagonal, anti-time-ordering and involution. No positivity of formal coefficients is assumed.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

A.title: Scalar Epstein–Glaser induction at finite perturbative order
A.statement: For the stated free scalar polynomial algebra, time-ordered products satisfying the scalar contract can be constructed at every finite order; at each graph order the extension ambiguity is a finite linear combination of derivatives of delta distributions on relevant diagonals, bounded by the specified scaling degree. This yields a formal series, with no convergence or adiabatic limit assertion.
A.proof_route: Induct in n: causal-order open sets cover the complement of the total diagonal; lower-order factorizations agree on overlaps by associativity/locality. Glue using a locally finite partition of unity, reduce to relative coordinates, extend each numerical distribution by the scaling-degree theorem, symmetrize and impose scalar normalization conditions. Prove the needed finite graph scaling bounds using derivative kernel estimates. Partial diagonals are already resolved by the induction, not independently multiplied. Lorentz covariance needs the finite-dimensional cocycle correction proved locally; include it as part of this theorem proof rather than assume it.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

A.title: Renormalization maps form a formal composition group
A.statement: Given two admissible scalar time-ordered systems S and S′ with the same first-order normalization, there is a unique local formal map Z(V)=V+O(V²), Z(0)=0, Z′(0)=id, such that S′=S∘Z. Composition and recursively defined formal inverse preserve the local support and normalization conditions.
A.proof_route: At homogeneous order n subtract all known lower partitions; the difference is supported on the total diagonal. Define Z_n to be that local difference with exact factorial conventions. Composition uses finite partitions of n, hence is coefficientwise finite. Invert recursively, showing the leading unknown occurs linearly.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

B.title: Two-vertex scalar logarithm and its local ambiguity
B.statement: In four dimensions the two-vertex four-point scalar graph has scaling degree four in its relative variable; its renormalized extension may differ by cδ. The scale difference is local, not a numerical scattering probability.

pairs.title: Rooted forests, Hopf antipodes and subtraction recursion

A.title: Admissible-cut Hopf algebra for subdivergence forests
A.statement: H is the polynomial algebra over Q on finite nonempty rooted trees, graded by vertices. Δ(t)=t⊗1+1⊗t+Σ_c P_c(t)⊗R_c(t), summing cuts with at most one cut edge on each root-to-leaf path; extend Δ multiplicatively. ε kills positive degree. This is a rooted-tree subtraction model, not an automatic Hopf algebra of every gauge graph.
A.proof_route: Define the empty forest unit, trunk and pruned forest, and distinguish full cut from empty cut to avoid double counting.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

A.title: Admissible cuts give coassociativity and recursive antipode
A.statement: The rooted-forest coproduct is coassociative and H is a connected graded bialgebra. Its antipode is S(t)=−t−Σ_c S(P_c(t))R_c(t), extended by the convolution inverse, and this recursion terminates in every fixed degree.
A.proof_route: Identify iterated coproduct terms with two-level nested prunings of a tree; both orders encode the same three layers. All proper factors have fewer vertices, so degree induction yields both convolution inverse identities. Prove multiplicativity of the antipode in the commutative case.
A.design_status: planned; proof route is an authoring obligation, not accepted proof

A.title: Subtraction characters and forest cancellation
A.statement: Let A=A_-⊕A_+ be a commutative Laurent-series algebra split into negative powers and nonnegative powers, with projection R onto A_-. For a character φ:H→A, set φ_-(t)=−R[φ(t)+Σ_c φ_-(P_c(t))φ(R_c(t))] and φ_+=φ_-*φ. Then φ_- and φ_+ are characters, φ_+ takes positive-degree values in A_+, and the recursion is degreewise finite.
A.proof_route: Verify R(a)R(b)=R(R(a)b+aR(b)−ab) directly by the Laurent splitting. Use this identity and the multiplicative coproduct to prove by degree induction that the recursion preserves products. Expand φ_+ and cancel the negative part; this is the exact Hopf utilization in subtraction, without importing an unproved full Feynman-graph identification.

B.title: Nested subdivergence has a nontrivial convolution counterterm
B.statement: For the two-vertex ladder t with one proper cut and one-vertex tree τ, φ_-(t)=−R(φ(t)+φ_-(τ)φ(τ)); subtracting only Rφ(t) generally differs.
B.proof_route: Choose φ(τ)=a/ε+b and φ(t)=c/ε²+d/ε+e and calculate the a²/ε² and ab/ε corrections explicitly.

pairs.title: Off-shell gauge complexes, BRST doublets and anomaly obstructions

A.title: Abelian local jet BRST differential
A.statement: On the graded-commutative algebra of finite jets of a U(1) connection A, odd ghost c, antighost cbar and even auxiliary B, define sA=dc, sc=0, scbar=B,sB=0, and commute s with spacetime derivatives. On a charged matter field ψ of charge q set sψ=iqcψ and use the graded Leibniz rule. Work off shell with explicit ghost numbers.
A.proof_route: Specify coefficients as smooth functions of spacetime and finite polynomial jet dependence. A state-space charge is not part of this algebra.

A.title: Nilpotence and contraction of nonminimal doublets
A.statement: The stated Abelian s squares to zero. Adjoining finitely many jet doublets su=v,sv=0 independent of the other transformations does not change polynomial BRST cohomology: every closed expression of strictly positive doublet degree is exact.
A.proof_route: On generators s²A=dsc=0, s²ψ=iq(sc)ψ−iqc(iqcψ)=0 because c²=0. Define h=u∂_v with graded derivatives and N counting doublet jets; sh+hs=N. Decompose finite polynomials by N-degree; closed a_k with k>0 equals s(h a_k/k). Carry ghost parity in every derivative.

A.title: Wess–Zumino consistency is an obstruction class
A.statement: If a nilpotent BRST Ward identity first fails at formal order ℏ^n by a local ghost-number-one integrated functional A, the nilpotence identity forces sA=0 modulo total derivatives. A local counterterm cancels this failure exactly when [A]=0 in H^1(s|d), with the sign fixed by the chosen Ward convention.
A.proof_route: Expand the squared Ward differential at the first failing order; lower-order failures vanish. A counterterm changes A by sB+dC. Conversely a cohomologically trivial representative supplies that counterterm. This proves the obstruction principle conditional on locality of the breaking; the quantum action principle is an additional theorem obligation in a gauge model, not a consequence of scalar extension.

B.statement: If sa=0 and a has doublet degree two, then a=s(ha/2). This is not a proof that all physical ghost-number-zero classes have positive Hilbert norm.

pairs.title: Current-algebra cocycles and conditional chiral anomaly cancellation

A.title: Loop current Lie algebra and central term
A.statement: For a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g with invariant symmetric form κ, let Lg=C∞(S¹,g) with pointwise bracket and define ω(X,Y)=(1/2π)∫_0^{2π}κ(X,∂θY)dθ. The central extension has bracket [(X,a),(Y,b)]=([X,Y],ω(X,Y)).

A.statement: ω is antisymmetric and ω([X,Y],Z)+ω([Y,Z],X)+ω([Z,X],Y)=0. Hence the central bracket obeys Jacobi.
A.proof_route: Integrate ∂θκ(X,Y) to zero for antisymmetry. Use invariance and the Leibniz rule to express the cyclic sum as ∂θκ(X,[Y,Z]); its integral vanishes. Check the original g Jacobi and central coordinate independently.

A.statement: For a specified four-dimensional left-handed Weyl matter content in representations R_i, define d^{abc}=Σ_i tr_{R_i}(T^a{T^b,T^c}). An anomaly-cancellation statement requires a regulator/renormalization construction that identifies the local consistent anomaly with the descent class of this tensor, specifies mixed gravitational and global anomalies separately, and carries all loop hypotheses. pairs.title: Gaussian matching and a rigorous derivative-expansion remainder

A.title: Positive heavy-mode Gaussian matching data
A.statement: Let K be a positive self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space with spectrum in [M²,∞), M>0, and let J be a vector. In a finite regulator, integrate a real Gaussian heavy coordinate χ with quadratic action 〈χ,Kχ〉/2−〈J,χ〉. Its normalized elimination contributes −〈J,K^{-1}J〉/2 to the effective action. Determinants are finite-regulator quantities. AC is retained through the spectral-calculus supplier.

A.title: Low-momentum matching has a controlled remainder
A.statement: Let K=M²+A with A≥0 self-adjoint and J in its spectral subspace 0≤A≤E². For N≥0, K^{-1}J=M^{-2}Σ_{r=0}^N(−A/M²)^rJ+R_NJ, with ||R_NJ||≤M^{-2}(E²/M²)^{N+1}||J||. Consequently the induced quadratic-action remainder is at most ||J||²( E²/M²)^{N+1}/(2M²). AC is inherited from the analytic construction suppliers.
A.proof_route: Use the scalar identity (1+x)^{-1}=Σ_{r=0}^N(−x)^r+(−x)^{N+1}/(1+x), then spectral calculus on the finite low-energy band. Bound 1/(1+x)≤1 for x≥0; no asymptotic assumption is required for the identity, but usefulness requires E/M<1.

pairs.title: Spinor helicity, rational factorization and tree recursion

A.statement: For a complex null four-momentum in the explicitly translated effective Clifford metric −η, the 2×2 momentum matrix has rank one and factorizes as λ_a λtilde_adot. The rescaling (λ,λtilde)↦(tλ,t^{-1}λtilde), t≠0, leaves momentum invariant. An outgoing helicity-h amplitude has weight t^{-2h}. Angle and square brackets use fixed alternating tensors.

A.statement: Let A(z) be a rational shifted tree amplitude, regular at z=0, with only simple finite factorization poles z_i and A(z)→0 as z→∞. Then A(0)=−Σ_i Res_{z=z_i} A(z)/z. If each residue is the stated product of lower-point on-shell amplitudes divided by the propagator derivative and summed over internal helicities, this gives BCFW recursion. A boundary term is required when decay fails.

pairs.title: Soft coherent radiation, resolution and inclusive cancellation

A.title: Independent soft-radiation resolution model
A.statement: For an explicitly prescribed conserved eikonal current and cutoffs 0<ε<Δ<Λ, take a free-photon coherent state whose mode intensity is dν=C dω/ω on the selected angular region, C≥0. Counts in disjoint frequency intervals are independent Poisson variables. Δ is a detector resolution in this model.

A.statement: Assume AC. If A is densely defined nonnegative self-adjoint on H, B=(I+A)^{-1} is a bounded positive self-adjoint injection with dense range. A.statement: For a finite-dimensional complex module V of the semisimple real Lie algebra so(1,3), a Lie-algebra 1-cocycle c satisfying c([X,Y])=X·c(Y)−Y·c(X) is of the form c(X)=X·v for some v∈V.
